name: Dean Wallace

tenures.note: Challenged Doctor David Chambers for the Evo Title at Dawning, losing by submission (41:02) after a three-match losing skein against him. Coaches a youth baseball team in Tempe, AZ in his own downtime, including two autistic players and a boy in a wheelchair he treats as a father figure ("Step Nine: Reason" — the children and their guardian are not separately registered, pure biographical color). A younger brother, Ryan Wallace, is a recurring comic foil across three Legends Board pieces.

Billed teaming with Frank Heimdal against The Trents on the Thursday Tempest card of 9 August 2001; named by Joe Black on Black Talk that December as one of two newcomers who "greatly exceeded" expectations.

caption: "The Closer", who spent his own roleplays coaching a children's baseball team in Tempe and met Doctor David Chambers for the Evo Championship at Dawning.

name: Doctor David Chambers

tenures.note: Evo Champion by Dawning, retaining there over Dean Wallace (submission, 41:02) and earlier at Impulse 1.9 over Brad Case (No Contest, Dean Wallace interference); named Michael Gabrielle the #1 contender at the close of Impulse 2.1. Captured, tortured for three days, and eventually freed from Duel/Alex Lawson, Aaron Antioch/Lost, and Mike Static ("Mike and Aaron and their rat-bastard buddy") at "the Asylum"; convalesces afterward at Olivia Heimdal's own house ("Life at the Heimdals Part 1").

Interviewed on Late Night Lethal as "The Doctor", debuting with the gimmick of speaking only through a stuffed bear, forming The Asylum with the newly-renamed Aaron Antioch; a later Late Night Lethal episode has a returning guest recall a "memorable two-part series" with "David Chambers and Aaron Antioch", tying the masked gimmick to this already-registered name.

caption: The Evo Champion of 2002, announced to "Chop Suey!" and out of the elevator in a black leather jacket and hospital scrubs with Bear the Bear in tow.

name: Duel

tenures.source: promotions/lcw-evo/archive/evo-dawning-15-match-6-madhouse-title-cage-match-duel-c.html; the federation's own Legends Board and its served show segments (promotions/lcw-evo/)
tenures.note: Real name Alexander "Alex" Lawson, a Philadelphian who scouted the Club Evo site himself. His own "Solitude" RP narrates the full backstory: repressed emotion since his father's 1981 death fractured into a dissociative alter-ego calling itself "Felony" in early 2001 (the same Felony gravity-lcw's own tenure note already cites alongside Mike Static as having "terrorized LCW" — the same man, not a second character); severe head trauma that April led to a second alter, "Duel," from June 2001. Won the (then-"neo") Title from Rook Black by choke-out, per the Dawning Match 6 video-package recap text — which oddly calls it an "Evo Title match" rather than naming the belt outright, quoted verbatim rather than silently normalized (see data/reigns.json). Held the Hardcore/Madhouse Title from the split itself through Dawning, where Frank Heimdal ends the reign in a cage (32:14). A documented relationship with Olivia Heimdal ends sometime before Dawning ("Solitude").

Billed in a singles match against Apex on the Thursday Tempest card of 9 August 2001; the results page was never captured. Per "Solitude" (lcw-evo), this is the debut of the "Felony" alter-ego that would go on to terrorize LCW as part of the Black Dogs alongside Mike Static, before a head injury and the "Duel" identity replaced it in mid-2001.

tenures.note: Leads the Tribulation Saints with Lost/Aaron Antioch (win over Pheonyx/Gryfon at Impulse 1.9); named #1 contender to Doctor David Chambers' Evo Title at the close of Impulse 2.1's "Messiah's Challenge." Not added to aka[] (same common-word auto-link risk as "Lost," kept prose-only).

Billed on Late Night Lethal as Aaron Antioch's cousin and tag partner in Divine Intervention, addressed there only as Angel; took time off to marry Danielle (billed as Destiny) and returned under a new name, Lunacy, once the team's storyline moved on. This pass's own read of "The Michael Gabrielle Saga" (chapters 4-5, Evo's own Legends Board) narrates a different, earlier college-era fiancée at UT Austin, Victoria Marie Brice ("Vicky"), who leaves him once his plan to recruit Aaron becomes clear — kept alongside the existing "Danielle" citation above, unresolved, a genuine period-document inconsistency rather than a silently-picked answer. Also called Aaron/Lost's "nephew" once (rather than cousin) in "Father's Day Comes Early This Year" — likewise left as an inconsistency, not corrected.
